docs.text: Acute myeloid leukemia ≥20% myeloid blasts — or any blast % with a defining genetic lesion · classification and treatment are now genetically driven · every new diagnosis is triaged for the three emergencies before a regimen is chosen Compiled from the Encyclopedia AML review note and Fellowship Anki deck · ELN 2022 · WHO 2022 / ICC · NCCN. Diagnosis ≥20% myeloid blasts — or any blast % with a defining fusion : t(8;21), inv(16)/t(16;16), PML::RARA. WHO 2022 also drops it for NPM1 but keeps ≥20% for CEBPA-bZIP ; ICC sets ≥10% for both Also AML at <20%: myeloid sarcoma / extramedullary disease “Blasts” on smear is morphologic — confirm lineage by flow Workup: marrow aspirate + biopsy with flow, karyotype + FISH, NGS ; CBC/smear (Auer rods); coags + fibrinogen + D-dimer ; TLS labs; baseline echo ; HLA typing early; LP only for CNS symptoms (consider if monocytic), after coags corrected Stat FISH/PCR for PML::RARA on any suspicion of APL Median age ~68. The three triage questions on every new AML: Is it APL? Is there leukostasis? Is there tumor lysis? ELN 2022 genetic risk Risk Representative genetics Favorable t(8;21) RUNX1::RUNX1T1 · inv(16)/t(16;16) CBFB::MYH11 ( core-binding factor ) · mutated NPM1 without FLT3-ITD · in-frame bZIP CEBPA Intermediate NPM1 + FLT3-ITD · wild-type NPM1 + FLT3-ITD · t(9;11) MLLT3::KMT2A · anything not otherwise classified Adverse Complex or monosomal karyotype · −5/del(5q), −7, abn(17p) · TP53 · MDS-related genes (ASXL1, BCOR, EZH2, RUNX1, SF3B1, SRSF2, STAG2, U2AF1, ZRSR2) · KMT2A rearrangements except t(9;11) and KMT2A-PTD · t(6;9), inv(3) ELN 2022 changes worth knowing: FLT3-ITD is intermediate regardless of allelic ratio (ratio dropped) · only in-frame bZIP CEBPA is favorable · NPM1 with adverse cytogenetics is reclassified adverse · KIT co-mutation worsens CBF-AML prognostically, but ELN 2022 kept it favorable . Genotype → phenotype FLT3-ITD Hyperleukocytosis; normal karyotype. ↑ CNS risk , most when NPM1 co-mutated KMT2A / 11q23 Monocytic — gum hypertrophy, leukemia cutis. Highest multivariable odds for CNS disease (OR ~7.6) t(8;21) Myeloid sarcoma ; aberrant CD19 / CD56 by flow inv(16) Abnormal marrow eosinophils with coarse basophilic granules (FAB M4Eo) TP53 Complex karyotype, t-AML; venetoclax-resistant , poor outcome even after allo DTA DNMT3A, TET2, ASXL1 persist in CR as clonal hematopoiesis — not MRD markers CNS disease is uncommon — ~0.6% at diagnosis, ~3% at relapse . Risk factors differ by series: SAL (n=3,261) found FLT3-ITD ± NPM1 ; another found 11q23 (OR 7.6) and WBC ≥100k on multivariable analysis. Treatment pathway First: exclude APL, then assess fitness Before committing to a regimen APL must be excluded — ATRA cannot wait 7+3 may start while NGS pends, but FLT3 status changes induction — hold a day or two if stable; instability forces faster action Fit for intensive therapy Induction — 7+3 cytarabine ×7 days + anthracycline ×3 FLT3-mutated: add midostaurin (RATIFY) CD33 / CBF: add gemtuzumab (ALFA-0701) secondary or t-AML: consider CPX-351 PARADIGM (2026) adverse risk and not FLT3-mutated : aza+ven EFS 14.5 vs 6.2 mo , HR 0.57. Less infection and bleeding, and more patients reached allo phase 2, EFS endpoint — OS not significantly different Assess response day-14 marrow ; residual disease → re-induce goal is CR: blasts <5% with count recovery Consolidation by ELN risk favorable → HiDAC ×3–4 cycles, no allo intermediate / adverse → allo-HSCT in CR1 MRD-positive CR pushes toward transplant If not going to transplant oral azacitidine (CC-486) maintenance QUAZAR: OS 24.7 vs 14.8 months Unfit for intensive therapy Venetoclax + azacitidine VIALE-A : OS 14.7 vs 9.6 months vs aza alone watch TLS on ramp-up ; reduce dose with azoles IDH1-mutant alternative: ivosidenib + aza (AGILE) Relapsed / refractory Target first, then salvage FLT3 → gilteritinib (ADMIRAL) IDH1/2 → ivosidenib / enasidenib KMT2A-r or NPM1 → menin inhibitor salvage chemo: FLAG-IDA, MEC, CLAG-M Regimens & agents Regimen Notes 7+3 Cytarabine infusion ×7 days + an anthracycline ×3 — the backbone for fit patients. Daunorubicin 60 mg/m² is the modern standard: E1900 showed 90 > 45 , but AML17 found 90 vs 60 gave no CR or OS benefit and doubled 60-day mortality + midostaurin FLT3-mutated (RATIFY). Quizartinib for FLT3-ITD (QuANTUM-First) + gemtuzumab Fractionated dosing (ALFA-0701 — no CD33 cutoff). CBF benefit comes from the Hills meta-analysis , not ALFA-0701 CPX-351 Liposomal cytarabine + daunorubicin for t-AML / AML-MRC. Caveat: comparator was 7+3, not ven/aza — niche today is the fitter older adult bridging to allo HiDAC 3 g/m² q12h on days 1, 3, 5 ×3–4 cycles; best in CBF. Age >60 → IDAC 1.5 g/m² — 3 g/m² is inappropriate (ocular, cerebellar, infectious toxicity). Renal dose-reduce Venetoclax + azacitidine Unfit patients (VIALE-A). Ramp-up with TLS prophylaxis; reduce venetoclax with CYP3A inhibitors This table is when and why . Every regimen's dosing lives on page 3 — the two HiDAC numbers stay here because the dose is the teaching point. MRD and the transplant decision Measure MRD at the end of every cycle and again before transplant — order HemeSTAMP MRD (NGS) + multiparameter flow cytometry ; add NPM1 PCR where applicable MRD-positive CR is not CR for planning purposes — it predicts relapse and moves an otherwise favorable-risk patient toward transplant Allo-HSCT in CR1: generally not for favorable risk · yes for intermediate and adverse risk · modified by MRD, age, comorbidity, and donor availability Allo cures through graft-versus-leukemia . Auto-HSCT lacks GVL and relapses more — niche for MRD-negative CR1 without a donor Fitness for intensive therapy is a composite of age, performance status and comorbidity (HCT-CI) — not age alone The three emergencies APL Recognize DIC + bleeding + hypergranular promyelocytes bundled Auer rods microgranular variant can look monocytic Start ATRA immediately do not wait for PML::RARA — hemorrhage is the leading cause of APL death, and it is preventable 45 mg/m²/day PO divided q12h (22.5 mg/m² BID); a one-time dose overnight is fine Support aggressively fibrinogen >100 (cryo), platelets >30k , INR <2 coags q6–8 h; avoid LP and central lines Risk-stratify, then treat Sanz: low = WBC ≤10k and plt >40k · intermediate = WBC ≤10k and plt ≤40k · high = WBC >10k ATRA + arsenic , chemo-free, for low/intermediate high risk: add anthracycline (or GO) cure >90%; do NOT leukapherese — worsens DIC Leukostasis Hyperleukocytosis + symptoms myeloid blasts are large and sticky — symptoms at lower counts than ALL/CLL, often >50–100k CNS (headache, confusion, vision) + pulmonary (hypoxia) Management — with doses hydroxyurea up to 2 g PO q6h , goal WBC <20k literature 50–100 mg/kg/day; mucositis ≥75 mg/kg/day HU takes days — if too slow, cytarabine 1 g ×1 urgent induction is definitive ; leukapheresis if severe — never in APL , no mortality benefit. No RBC transfusion hydrate + TLS ppx. dex 10 mg IV q6h if monocytic + ARF Tumor lysis Cairo-Bishop lab TLS = ≥2 of ↑K, ↑phosphate, ↑uric acid, ↓Ca clinical TLS = lab TLS + AKI, arrhythmia or seizure Prevent and treat aggressive IV hydration is the cornerstone allopurinol 300 mg BID standard risk rasburicase if high risk or uric acid >8 — not in G6PD no urinary alkalinization Drug toxicity & monitoring Agent Watch for Cytarabine Pyrimidine analog. High-dose: cerebellar toxicity — cerebellar exam before every HiDAC dose, hold if abnormal ; conjunctivitis → prophylactic steroid eye drops ; ara-C syndrome (fever, myalgia, rash) Anthracyclines Cumulative, dose-dependent cardiotoxicity — track total dose, baseline ± serial LVEF. Vesicant — central access Venetoclax Tumor lysis on ramp-up ; neutropenia; dose-reduce with azole antifungals (CYP3A) Azacitidine vs decitabine Both hypomethylating; azacitidine incorporates into RNA and DNA , decitabine DNA-only. Azacitidine: injection-site reactions Gemtuzumab Anti-CD33 calicheamicin ADC — hepatotoxicity and VOD/SOS , especially peri-transplant; fractionated dosing lowers risk Arsenic trioxide QT prolongation — monitor ECG, replete K and Mg Differentiation syndrome ATRA/ATO and also IDH and menin inhibitors . Fever, dyspnea, hypoxia, infiltrates, effusions, weight gain, AKI → dexamethasone 10 mg IV BID at first suspicion Menin inhibitors Revumenib, ziftomenib — differentiation syndrome + QT prolongation Trial evidence RATIFY Midostaurin + 7+3 in FLT3-mutated — survival benefit QuANTUM-First Quizartinib + 7+3 in FLT3-ITD ALFA-0701 Fractionated gemtuzumab + 7+3 — EFS/RFS benefit held in the final analysis but OS was no longer significant . Hills meta-analysis (n=3,325) is what shows the favorable-cytogenetics benefit: 5-yr OS +20.7% E1900 Daunorubicin 90 vs 45 mg/m² — better CR and OS in age <60 AML17 Daunorubicin 90 vs 60 mg/m² — no CR or OS difference , and 60-day mortality 10% vs 5% (HR 1.98). Read with E1900: 60 is standard, not 90 (Burnett, Blood 2015) VIALE-A Azacitidine + venetoclax vs azacitidine — OS 14.7 vs 9.6 months (DiNardo, NEJM 2020) PARADIGM Aza+ven vs intensive induction in fit patients (CBF/FLT3/NPM1<60 excluded, 72% ELN adverse): EFS 14.5 vs 6.2 mo , HR 0.57; less infection and bleeding. Phase 2; OS not significant (Fathi, NEJM 2026) AGILE Ivosidenib + azacitidine in IDH1-mutant unfit patients ADMIRAL Gilteritinib in relapsed FLT3-mutated AML — survival benefit SORMAIN Sorafenib maintenance after allo in FLT3-ITD AML — 24-mo RFS 85% vs 53% , HR 0.39. Phase 2, n=83; off-label (Burchert, JCO 2020) MORPHO Gilteritinib maintenance after allo in FLT3-ITD, n=356. RFS missed overall (HR 0.68, P=0.052) — but benefit in the half who were MRD-positive pre- or post-HCT (HR 0.52, P=0.007) and none if MRD-negative . An MRD-guided decision (Levis, JCO 2024) APL0406 ATRA + arsenic beat ATRA + chemo in low/intermediate-risk APL (Lo-Coco, NEJM 2013) QUAZAR AML-001 Oral azacitidine (CC-486) maintenance in CR1 — OS 24.7 vs 14.8 months AML15 IDAC vs HiDAC consolidation — no overall survival difference SWOG S1203 IA regimen showed no benefit and more toxicity — 7+3 remains standard Genetics — fine points inv(3) / t(3;3) MECOM (EVI1, 3q26) activation; classically normal or high platelets ; adverse and venetoclax-resistant t(6;9) DEK::NUP214 — associates with FLT3-ITD and basophilia ; adverse NPM1 flow mimic NPM1-mutated AML can be HLA-DR− / CD34− and mimic APL — confirm PML::RARA Therapy-related After alkylators/RT : del(5q)/del(7q) ± TP53, latency ~5–7 yr. After topoisomerase-II : 11q23 KMT2A , latency ~2–3 yr Germline DDX41, RUNX1, CEBPA, GATA2 , telomere biology — send germline testing if young, family history, or multiple cytopenias; it changes related-donor selection Four ways an acute leukemic dies in the ED 1. Leukostasis — CVA, MI, respiratory failure 2. Bleeding / DIC / thrombosis 3. Infection — very low threshold for broad-spectrum antibiotics 4. Tumor lysis — renal failure, electrolyte derangement Overnight decisions 1. Triage floor vs ICU — leukapheresis and CRRT both require ICU 2. Rule out APL — start ATRA on any suspicion , do not wait for PML::RARA 3. Cytoreduction — see doses at right 4. TLS — start fluids + allopurinol, set lab frequency ( q4h to daily ). Rasburicase if uric acid >8: 0.15–0.2 mg/kg IV , in adults usually a single dose capped at 6 mg (label allows 0.2 mg/kg daily ×5 days). Check G6PD — contraindicated if deficient Supportive care Transfusion: platelets >10k (>20–50k if bleeding, procedure, or APL); irradiated and leukoreduced products Prophylaxis during induction: levofloxacin 500 mg PO daily · posaconazole DR 300 mg BID ×1 day, then 300 mg daily · acyclovir 400 mg PO BID (HSV-seropositive) Posaconazole is a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor — that is what forces the venetoclax reduction: 400 mg → 70 mg daily with posaconazole (100 mg with other strong inhibitors such as voriconazole), during ramp-up and beyond Hepatitis B: screen HBsAg + anti-HBc before therapy. HBsAg-positive → entecavir or tenofovir (preferred over lamivudine) for any systemic anticancer therapy, continued ≥12 months past the last cycle. Isolated anti-HBc-positive → prophylax or monitor HBV DNA closely; AML chemotherapy carries reactivation risk similar to lymphoma Febrile neutropenia: fever ≥38.3°C once (or ≥38.0°C for 1 h) with ANC <500 → cefepime 2 g IV q8h within 1 hour . Add vancomycin for hemodynamic instability, line infection, skin/soft tissue infection, pneumonia or known MRSA. Severe mucositis is a softer trigger than it looks — IDSA lists it only when fluoroquinolone prophylaxis was used and ceftazidime is the empiric agent (viridans strep); cefepime already covers viridans strep . Antifungal if fever persists >4–7 days Fertility counseling before chemotherapy; central venous access; early palliative care in older or adverse-risk disease What to send Test When Peripheral studies Flow cytometry , AML prognosis assay (NPM1, FLT3-ITD, FLT3-TKD), IDH mutation analysis . Send if WBC >10k and marrow will be delayed, or the patient is old enough that you would rather not subject them to a marrow Cytogenetics FISH for PML::RARA and BCR::ABL1 . Send from peripheral blood if there is any concern for APL or a delay in getting marrow HLA typing Send if the patient is a possible allogeneic transplant candidate Cytoreduction overnight Dose and trigger Hydroxyurea Consider if WBC >20k . Overnight you can order a one-time dose . Typical range 500 mg–2 g , max 2 g q6h . Literature range 50–100 mg/kg/day; grade 3–4 mucositis rises at ≥75 mg/kg/day , so 2 g q6h is the ceiling, not the starting dose Leukapheresis Consider for evidence of leukostasis — headache, blurry vision, dyspnea/hypoxia, chest pain — typically with blasts >50k in AML (rare in ALL). Page apheresis 12027. Ask ER or the MICU triage fellow for a trialysis line ; admit to MICU. Ask the apheresis RN to save the product in the FGR fridge and coordinate with the research team. Never in APL Cytarabine 1 g ×1 may be considered for leukostasis when apheresis will be delayed APL overnight Start ATRA on any concern for APL — do not wait for PML::RARA Smear: bilobed / folded nuclei ± Auer rods. Page pathology on call (12005) if unsure ATRA 45 mg/m²/day PO divided q12h (= 22.5 mg/m² BID) — overnight you can give a one-time dose DIC labs q6–8h. Transfuse platelets >30 , fibrinogen >100 , INR <2 Regimen dosing Regimen Dosing 7+3 Cytarabine 100–200 mg/m²/day IV continuous infusion ×7 days from day 1 ( SHC uses 100 ) + daunorubicin 60 mg/m² IV daily days 1–3 schedule E1900; 60 vs 90 from AML17 7+3 + GO Add gemtuzumab ozogamicin 3 mg/m² (max 4.5 mg) IV over 2 h on days 1, 4, 7 ALFA-0701 / Lambert 2019 7+3 + midostaurin Add midostaurin 50 mg PO q12h on days 8–21 RATIFY / Stone 2017 CPX-351 Liposomal daunorubicin 44 mg/m² + cytarabine 100 mg/m² IV on days 1, 3, 5 Lancet 2018 FLAG-IDA-VEN Fludarabine 30 mg/m² + cytarabine 1.5–2 g/m² IV days 2–6; idarubicin IV ( ND-AML 8 mg/m² days 4–6 ; R/R 6 mg/m² days 4–5 ); filgrastim 5 mcg/kg days 1–7; venetoclax ramp-up (100/200/400 mg) days 1–14 DiNardo 2021 CLAD / LDAC / VEN Cladribine 5 mg/m² IV days 1–5 + cytarabine 20 mg/m² (SQ BID days 1–10; 20 mg/m² IV daily preferred at SHC ) + venetoclax PO days 1–21, alternating with azacitidine Kadia 2022 MEC Mitoxantrone 6–8 mg/m² + etoposide 80–100 mg/m² + cytarabine 1 g/m² , all daily days 1–5 (some series run 6 days) — dosing varies by protocol, check yours relapsed / refractory CLAG-M Cladribine 5 mg/m² IV days 1–5 + cytarabine 2 g/m² IV days 1–5 + mitoxantrone 10 mg/m² IV days 1–3 + G-CSF 300 mcg days 0–5 relapsed / refractory HMA / VEN Venetoclax (ramp-up) daily ×28 days + decitabine 20 mg/m² days 1–5 or azacitidine 75 mg/m² days 1–7 VIALE-A / DiNardo 2020 APL induction — dosing Regimen Dosing ATO / ATRA Arsenic trioxide 0.15 mg/kg IV over 2 h daily from day 1 + ATRA 22.5 mg/m² PO BID from day 1 — both until hematologic CR or max 60 days APL0406 / Lo-Coco 2013 ATO / ATRA / IDA ATO 0.15 mg/kg IV days 9–36 + ATRA 22.5 mg/m² BID days 1–36 + idarubicin on days 2, 4, 6, 8 by age: ≤60 yr 12 mg/m² · 61–70 yr 9 mg/m² · >70 yr 6 mg/m² APML4 / Iland 2012 ATO / ATRA / GO ATO 0.3 mg/kg IV daily days 1–5, then 0.25 mg/kg twice weekly weeks 2–8 + ATRA 22.5 mg/m² BID from day 1 until CR or max 60 days + gemtuzumab 6 mg/m² IV once on day 1 — high risk only (WBC >10k) AML17 APL / Burnett 2015

docs.text: Biliary tract cancer Gallbladder · intrahepatic, perihilar and distal cholangiocarcinoma · one systemic backbone, four different operations, and a molecular profile that depends entirely on where the tumor sits Compiled from the Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Gallbladder Cancer and Cholangiocarcinoma (Northness A, Heestand G) · NCCN · primary trial reports and FDA actions verified against PubMed, September 2026. Four diseases in one name Site Notes Intrahepatic CCA ~10% of CCA Arises proximal to the second-order ducts. The molecularly rich one — FGFR2 and IDH1 live here Perihilar (Klatskin) ~40% of CCA At the confluence of the right and left hepatic ducts. Resection planned by Bismuth-Corlette class Distal CCA ~50% of CCA Common bile duct up to, but not including, the ampulla Gallbladder cancer <5,000 cases/yr US; fundus 60% > body 30% > neck 10%. 1–2% are found incidentally at cholecystectomy for stones ~8,000 cholangiocarcinomas/yr in the US, median age ~70. The subtypes share systemic therapy but differ in staging system, operation, and molecular profile — which is why anatomic site has to be stated before anything else. Risk: CCA — PSC, HBV/HCV, liver flukes, male sex, obesity, diabetes, alcohol. GBC — cholelithiasis, gallbladder calcification, female sex, chronic Salmonella or H. pylori infection. Workup Labs: CBC with differential, CMP, PT/INR, CA 19-9 , HBV and HCV serologies Imaging: triphasic CT abdomen/pelvis or liver-protocol MRI + CT chest to complete staging. PET/CT to exclude occult disease when the plan is resection Gallbladder: start with ultrasound — go to triphasic CT or MRI for a polyp >10 mm or wall thickening not explained by cholecystitis MRCP to plan biopsy and stenting. ERCP to stent, decompress and brush — brushings are often non-diagnostic, so go to EUS-FNA when they are Genomically profile every tumor , and send MMR, HER2 IHC and PD-L1 . This is not optional in biliary cancer — roughly a third of patients have a level 1/2 actionable alteration If perihilar CCA might go to transplant, do NOT perform a transperitoneal biopsy — tumor seeding disqualifies the patient from the protocol Treatment pathway Resectable Resection by anatomic site gallbladder T1a: cholecystectomy alone everything else: formal resection + lymphadenectomy Adjuvant therapy capecitabine ×8 cycles (BILCAP) is the default node-positive or margin-positive derive the clearest benefit — consider adding chemoradiation (SWOG S0809) Surveillance exam, CA 19-9 and triphasic CT C/A/P q3 months ×2 years , then q6 months Locally advanced, unresectable Systemic therapy first treat as metastatic — gem/cis + durvalumab or pembrolizumab Then consider local therapy no randomized evidence of survival benefit ablative RT gives excellent local control; ABC-07 was negative HAI floxuridine and Y-90 rest on single-arm phase 2 data Metastatic Start chemo-IO and profile in parallel gem/cis + durvalumab (TOPAZ-1) or + pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-966) — near-identical benefit, no biomarker send NGS, MMR and HER2 IHC on day one Second line targeted therapy if an alteration was found — see page 2 otherwise FOLFOX (ABC-06) Staging — three separate AJCC systems Site T staging hinges on Intrahepatic Size and vascular invasion: T1a ≤5 cm / T1b >5 cm, both without vascular invasion · T2 vascular invasion or multiple tumors · T3 perforates visceral peritoneum · T4 direct extrahepatic invasion. N is simply N0 / N1 Perihilar Depth then vessels: T1 confined to the duct · T2a into surrounding fat, T2b into hepatic parenchyma · T3 unilateral portal vein or hepatic artery branch · T4 main portal vein bilaterally, common hepatic artery, or second-order radicals with contralateral vessel Distal Millimetres of duct-wall invasion: T1 <5 mm · T2 5–12 mm · T3 >12 mm · T4 celiac axis, SMA or common hepatic artery Gallbladder Which side of the wall: T1a lamina propria, T1b muscularis · T2a peritoneal side, T2b hepatic side — the distinction drives the operation · T3 serosa, liver or one adjacent organ · T4 main portal vein / hepatic artery or ≥2 organs Nodes: perihilar, distal and gallbladder all use N1 = 1–3 nodes, N2 = ≥4 . Intrahepatic uses N0/N1 only. Surgery — the only curative option Most patients are unresectable at presentation, and most resected patients still recur Resectability requires: no retropancreatic or paraceliac nodes, no distant liver metastases, no main portal vein or hepatic artery invasion, no adjacent-organ invasion, no dissemination Intrahepatic → hepatic lobectomy; 5-yr OS 11–40%. Perihilar → en bloc resection by Bismuth-Corlette class. Distal → Whipple + extrahepatic duct; 5-yr OS 10–40% Gallbladder: T1a is cured by simple cholecystectomy alone. T1b and above need en bloc cholecystectomy + resection of liver segments 4a/4b + regional lymphadenectomy Incidentally discovered gallbladder cancer beyond T1a must go back to the operating room for the 4a/4b bed resection and lymphadenectomy Liver transplant is an option for highly selected perihilar CCA (Mayo protocol: mass ≤3 cm, no transperitoneal biopsy, no metastases) — intention-to-treat 5-yr survival ~53% Alteration by site — why site matters iCCA eCCA GBC FGFR2 fusion / rearrangement ~12% ~1% ~1–2% IDH1 ~20% ~1% ~1% IDH2 ~6% 0% ~0.5% HER2 / ERBB2 ~4% ~9% ~11–14% BRAF V600E ~3% ~0% ~0% KRAS, any ~12% ~38% ~10% MSI-H / dMMR ~1.5% ~4% ~2% BAP1 ~19% ~2% ~1% TP53 ~21% ~44% ~60% FGFR2 and IDH1 are intrahepatic diseases and are mutually exclusive. HER2 is a gallbladder and extrahepatic disease. Roughly a third of all biliary cancers carry a level 1/2 actionable alteration — but that is ~40% of intrahepatic versus ~15% of extrahepatic . Western cohorts (AACR GENIE); in East Asian series IDH1 and FGFR2 fall and KRAS rises. Living with an FGFR inhibitor Hyperphosphatemia is on-target , not idiosyncratic — FGFR1 blockade removes the FGF23 phosphaturic signal. It is a marker that the drug is working. Pemigatinib ~60%, futibatinib ~85%, lirafugratinib ~21% . Manage with a low-phosphate diet, sevelamer , and dose holds Ocular toxicity: serous retinopathy / retinal pigment epithelial detachment, plus dry eye in over 20%. Baseline and serial ophthalmology with OCT — roughly q2 months for 6 months, then q3 months Nail and hair: onycholysis in ~47%, alopecia in a third. Stomatitis, arthralgia and diarrhea are common Resistance arrives at ~6–9 months as polyclonal secondary FGFR2 kinase-domain mutations , classically the gatekeeper V564F . The covalent agents (futibatinib, lirafugratinib) retain activity against some but not all of these Driver → therapy Alteration Therapy FGFR2 fusion or rearrangement ~12% of iCCA All second-line and beyond. Lirafugratinib (FGFR2-selective; approved 23 Sep 2026 ) — ORR 46%, DOR 11.8 mo, and notably less hyperphosphatemia (~21%) . Futibatinib ORR 42% (accelerated; label is intrahepatic only ). Pemigatinib ORR 37% (accelerated, any site). Only fusions and rearrangements qualify — point mutations do not. FIGHT-302 moved pemigatinib to 1L on PFS but showed no OS gain , and the 1L indication is not approved. Infigratinib was withdrawn in 2024 IDH1 ~20% of iCCA Ivosidenib after 1–2 prior lines (regular approval). PFS 2.7 vs 1.4 months, HR 0.37 — statistically emphatic, clinically modest. Unadjusted OS was not significant (10.3 vs 7.5 mo) because 70% crossed over ; crossover-adjusted HR 0.49 HER2 GBC ~11–14%, eCCA ~9% Zanidatamab — the only BTC-specific approval (accelerated, Nov 2024), IHC 3+ only , 2L+: ORR 52% in IHC 3+, DOR 14.9 mo. T-DXd is covered by the tumor-agnostic IHC 3+ approval, but ILD reached 17% in the biliary cohort — higher than in most tumor types. Trastuzumab + pertuzumab is NCCN-listed but not FDA-approved here BRAF V600E ~3% of iCCA Dabrafenib + trametinib — tumor-agnostic accelerated approval. ROAR biliary cohort ORR 47–53%, PFS 9.0 mo MSI-H / dMMR ~1–3% Pembrolizumab (tumor-agnostic, now regular approval) — KEYNOTE-158 cholangiocarcinoma cohort ORR 41% , median OS 24.3 months. Dostarlimab is an alternative TMB ≥10 mut/Mb ~4% Pembrolizumab, tumor-agnostic accelerated approval NTRK or RET fusion <1% each Larotrectinib / entrectinib / repotrectinib for NTRK; selpercatinib for RET (tumor-agnostic, converted to traditional approval in 2026). Pralsetinib has no tumor-agnostic approval KRAS G12C ~1% No approved option in biliary cancer. Adagrasib showed activity in a small pan-tumor cohort (5/12); trial or off-label only Regimen dosing Regimen Dosing Gem/cis + durvalumab TOPAZ-1, 1L Gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² + cisplatin 25 mg/m² on days 1 and 8 , with durvalumab 1500 mg day 1 — q21d . Chemotherapy for up to 8 cycles, durvalumab continues Gem/cis + pembrolizumab KEYNOTE-966, 1L Same gem/cis backbone with pembrolizumab 200 mg day 1, q21d FOLFOX ABC-06, 2L Oxaliplatin 85 mg/m² day 1 + 5-FU 1200 mg/m²/day ×48 h continuous infusion from day 1 — q14d Gem + nab-paclitaxel Nab-paclitaxel 125 mg/m² then gemcitabine 1000 mg/m² , days 1, 8, 15 of a 28-day cycle . Single-arm phase 2 that missed its primary endpoint — an alternative, not a standard Adjuvant capecitabine BILCAP 1250 mg/m² PO twice daily, days 1–14 of a 21-day cycle, ×8 cycles (6 months). Grade 3 hand-foot in ~20% Adjuvant chemoRT SWOG S0809 Gemcitabine + capecitabine ×4 cycles, then capecitabine with radiation ×6 weeks (45 Gy nodal, 54–59.4 Gy tumor bed) Ivosidenib 500 mg PO daily — IDH1-mutant, after 1–2 prior lines Lirafugratinib 70 mg PO daily — FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement, previously treated, FGFR-inhibitor-naive Reading the adjuvant evidence honestly BILCAP is the standard of care but was a formally negative trial. ITT median OS 51.1 vs 36.4 months, HR 0.81, p=0.097 — the primary endpoint was not met . It became practice on the per-protocol analysis (HR 0.75) and a prespecified sensitivity analysis (HR 0.71). Worth knowing when someone asks why capecitabine SWOG S0809 is single-arm — 2-year OS 65% in resected extrahepatic CCA or gallbladder cancer with pT2-4, node-positive or margin-positive disease. Benchmark data, not a randomized comparison Negative adjuvant trials: PRODIGE-12 (GEMOX) and BCAT (gemcitabine) both failed. ASCOT showed adjuvant S-1 improves 3-year OS (77.1% vs 67.6%) in an all-Japanese population — but S-1 is not available in the US ACTICCA-1 (gem/cis vs capecitabine) has closed accrual and has not yet read out — it is the trial that may finally settle this Liver-directed therapy — what is actually supported Nothing randomized. Every option below rests on single-arm phase 2 or retrospective data HAI floxuridine via implanted pump (partial response 58%, median OS 25 months in a single-institution phase 2) — requires an experienced hepatobiliary program Y-90 / TARE concurrent with first-line chemotherapy: ORR 39%, median OS 22 months, 22% downstaged to surgery — but grade 3–4 toxicity was 71%, and the one randomized trial, SIRCCA, was terminated Ablative radiation gives excellent local control, but ABC-07 randomized SBRT after chemotherapy and missed its PFS endpoint (8.6 vs 9.0 months). The frequently quoted dose-escalation survival figures come from a retrospective series with heavy selection bias Key trials ABC-02 Gemcitabine + cisplatin vs gemcitabine — OS 11.7 vs 8.1 mo , HR 0.64. The backbone, since 2010 TOPAZ-1 Add durvalumab to gem/cis — OS 12.8 vs 11.5 mo, HR 0.80; 24-mo OS 24.9% vs 10.4% KEYNOTE-966 Add pembrolizumab to gem/cis — OS 12.7 vs 10.9 mo, HR 0.83. Effectively interchangeable with TOPAZ-1 ABC-06 FOLFOX after gem/cis — OS 6.2 vs 5.3 mo. Median gain is under a month; the honest number is 12-mo OS 25.9% vs 11.4% SWOG S1815 Adding nab-paclitaxel to gem/cis — negative . OS 14.0 vs 13.6 mo. Responses rose, survival did not BILCAP Adjuvant capecitabine — ITT p=0.097, primary endpoint not met ; standard of care on secondary analyses ASCOT Adjuvant S-1 , Japan — 3-yr OS 77.1% vs 67.6%. Not applicable in the US FIGHT-202 / FOENIX-CCA2 Pemigatinib (ORR 37%) and futibatinib (ORR 42%) in FGFR2-altered disease ReFocus Lirafugratinib — ORR 46%, DOR 11.8 mo, far less hyperphosphatemia. Approved 23 Sep 2026 ClarIDHy Ivosidenib in IDH1-mutant — PFS 2.7 vs 1.4 mo, HR 0.37 HERIZON-BTC-01 Zanidatamab in HER2 IHC 3+ — ORR 52%, DOR 14.9 mo ROAR Dabrafenib + trametinib in BRAF V600E — ORR 47–53%

docs.text: Breast cancer Every decision runs off subtype (HR+/HER2−, HER2+, TNBC) crossed with stage · AJCC 8th adds grade + ER/PR/HER2 as prognostic staging (does not apply pathologically after neoadjuvant therapy) Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Breast Cancer (Schultz C, Khan S, Sidhu K, Yang M, Dalal N, Tsai J) · NCCN 5.2025 · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter Workup Bilateral mammography + ultrasound; MRI or contrast-enhanced mammogram if indicated Core biopsy with clip placement Pathology: ER/PR, HER2 (IHC ± DISH — must do DISH if IHC 2+) , grade, Ki-67 “High risk”: HR weak/negative, HER2+, TNBC, high grade, Ki-67 >20% , inflammatory, angiosarcoma, malignant phyllodes Genetic testing : dx age ≤50 (NCCN) or ≤65 (ASCO) , bilateral at any age, or TNBC Stage I–IIB: no routine staging imaging — only if directed by signs, symptoms or labs Stage III: CT chest/abdomen ± pelvis + bone scan, or PET/CT Stage IV or recurrent: brain MRI if CNS symptoms, spine MRI if cord-compression symptoms, and biopsy the first recurrence — ideally a metastatic site Staging, margins & in-situ disease T1 / T2 / T3 ≤20 mm / >20–50 mm / >50 mm T4 chest wall (4a) · skin edema, ulceration, satellite nodules (4b) · both (4c) · 4d = inflammatory pN1 / pN2 / pN3 1–3 / 4–9 / ≥10 axillary nodes ; pN1mi = >0.2–2 mm; pN0(i+) = isolated tumor cells Negative margin ≥2 mm for DCIS and invasive; positive or close → discuss re-excision Post-neoadjuvant prefix yc / yp ; pathologic complete response = ypT0 ypN0 cM0 DCIS lumpectomy + whole-breast RT · or mastectomy ± SLN · or lumpectomy alone if small and age >70 . If ER+, tamoxifen × 5 yr (NSABP B-24) LCIS florid / pleomorphic → excise to negative margins; classical does not need negative margins Curative-intent pathway Local-regional and sequencing Standard sequence neoadjuvant (if indicated) → surgery → adjuvant chemo → radiation (± HER2 therapy) → endocrine therapy; may overlap Surgery choice BCS if clear margins + acceptable cosmesis mastectomy if not BCS-suitable, gene mutation, prior mantle RT, or patient preference Axilla omit SLNB if <2 cm, normal US, age ≥70 (SOUND) ALND if ≥3 positive nodes (Z0011), matted, inflammatory, or node-positive after neoadjuvant Adjuvant systemic by subtype HR+ / HER2− Oncotype DX on the surgical specimen chemo by recurrence score + menopausal status endocrine therapy for all HER2+ TCHP or TCH ×6; TH ×12 wk; AC→TH(P) complete 1 year (52 weeks) of trastuzumab residual disease → T-DM1 ×14 (KATHERINE) TNBC stage ≥II: KEYNOTE-522 regimen residual disease → capecitabine (CREATE-X) gBRCA + HER2−: olaparib × 1 yr (OlympiA) Neoadjuvant therapy — local-regional disease Subtype Neoadjuvant regimen If residual disease HR+ / HER2− ddAC → T , or TC ×4 — the same regimens used adjuvantly continue endocrine therapy ± CDK4/6 escalation HER2+ TCHP ×6 (preferred), or AC → THP T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg q21d ×14 (KATHERINE) TNBC, stage ≥II KEYNOTE-522 : carboplatin + paclitaxel + pembrolizumab → AC + pembrolizumab capecitabine ×6–8 (CREATE-X); if gBRCA, olaparib × 1 yr Indications: inflammatory or inoperable disease · T4 or N2–3 · TNBC or HER2+ with T2 or N1 · to downsize for breast conservation or downstage the axilla. T2/T3 meeting BCS criteria except for size → consider neoadjuvant. Response guides post-operative escalation — the main argument for treating first. † Oncotype DX — when to add chemotherapy Setting Recurrence score → recommendation Node-negative, any age RS 0–10 → endocrine therapy alone Node-negative, age >50 RS 11–25 → endocrine therapy alone; chemotherapy adds nothing Node-negative, age ≤50 RS 16–25 → consider adding chemotherapy — a real benefit in this group Node-negative, any age RS ≥26 → chemotherapy + endocrine therapy 1–3 nodes, postmenopausal RS ≤25 → endocrine therapy alone — no chemotherapy benefit 1–3 nodes, premenopausal RS ≤25 → chemotherapy still benefits 1–3 nodes, any RS >25 → chemotherapy + endocrine therapy Node-negative cutoffs from TAILORx (Sparano, NEJM 2018); node-positive from RxPONDER . Applies to ER/PR-positive, HER2-negative disease with up to 3 positive nodes; sent on the surgical specimen. † The handbook does not state these cutoffs — it defers to NCCN. Adjuvant escalation — HR+/HER2− Agent Regimen and eligibility Abemaciclib (monarchE) 150 mg BID × 2 years with endocrine therapy — ≥4 positive nodes , OR 1–3 nodes plus grade 3, tumor ≥5 cm, or Ki-67 ≥20% Ribociclib (NATALEE) 400 mg daily, 21 days on / 7 off × 3 years with endocrine therapy — any stage IIB or III, or stage IIA with grade 3 (or grade 2 with high genomic risk or Ki-67 ≥20%) Olaparib (OlympiA) 300 mg BID × 1 year — high-risk HER2-negative disease with a germline BRCA1/2 pathogenic variant Regimens & dosing Regimen Dosing Cycle ddAC → T doxorubicin 60 + cyclophosphamide 600 d1 → then paclitaxel 175 (or 80). Filgrastim d3–10 or pegfilgrastim d2 AC q14d ×4; then T q14d ×4 or q7d ×12 TC docetaxel 75 + cyclophosphamide 600 d1 q21d ×4 KEYNOTE-522 carboplatin AUC 5 d1 + paclitaxel 80 d1, 8, 15 + pembrolizumab 200 d1 → then doxorubicin 60 + cyclophosphamide 600 d1 q21d ×4 each; pembrolizumab × 1 year Capecitabine 1000–1250 mg/m² PO BID d1–14 q21d ×6–8 Trastuzumab 4 → 2 mg/kg weekly, or 8 → 6 mg/kg q3wk complete 52 weeks TCHP / TCH docetaxel 75 + carboplatin AUC 6 + trastuzumab 8→6 mg/kg (± pertuzumab 840→420) d1 q21d ×6 TH paclitaxel 80 weekly ×12 + trastuzumab 4→2 mg/kg weekly, then 6 mg/kg q3wk to 1 year q7d ×12 AC → TH(P) AC q14d ×4 → paclitaxel 80 weekly ×12 + trastuzumab ± pertuzumab to 1 year AC q14d ×4 T-DM1 3.6 mg/kg IV d1 — residual disease after preoperative therapy q21d ×14 All doses mg/m² unless stated. Avoid concurrent trastuzumab — especially trastuzumab + pertuzumab — with an anthracycline : significant cardiotoxicity. Cardiac monitoring every 3 months on trastuzumab. If T-DM1 is stopped for toxicity, give trastuzumab ± pertuzumab to complete 1 year. Bone-directed therapy Setting Agent and dose Bone metastases zoledronic acid 4 mg IV q4wk (may extend to q12wk after 12 months) · pamidronate 90 mg IV q3–4wk · denosumab 120 mg SQ q4wk Osteoporosis prevention denosumab 60 mg SQ q6 months · zoledronic acid 5 mg IV yearly · alendronate 70 mg PO weekly · calcium 1000 mg + vitamin D 800 IU daily Surveillance H&P every 6–12 months × 5 years, then annually Annual mammogram ; consider annual screening ultrasound if dense breast tissue, or CEM in lieu of mammogram + ultrasound Annual gynecologic assessment if on tamoxifen with a uterus Baseline DEXA before starting an aromatase inhibitor or after ovarian ablation, then every 1–2 years Assess and actively encourage adherence to endocrine therapy Lifestyle: alcohol <3 drinks/week, ≥150 min moderate exercise weekly, healthy BMI, Mediterranean diet DCIS: H&P + clinical breast exam q6 months × 5 years, mammogram q12 months Adjuvant endocrine therapy Premenopausal: tamoxifen 20 mg/d × 5–10 years — 5 years cuts recurrence 40% and death 30%; extending to 10 years cuts recurrence a further 25% and mortality 29% Add ovarian suppression if high risk — goserelin 3.6 mg SQ q4wk, leuprolide 3.75 mg monthly, or oophorectomy (SOFT) Postmenopausal: aromatase inhibitor × 5–10 years — anastrozole 1 mg, letrozole 2.5 mg (non-steroidal), exemestane 25 mg (steroidal) daily. Switch class if intolerant ; tamoxifen if AI contraindicated Tamoxifen is a CYP2D6 prodrug — avoid paroxetine and fluoxetine (also quinidine, cimetidine); citalopram and venlafaxine are acceptable. CYP2D6 genotyping is not recommended Menopause = prior bilateral oophorectomy, age ≥60, or <60 with amenorrhea ≥12 months off chemo/tamoxifen/ovarian suppression and postmenopausal FSH + estradiol Metastatic pathway Metastatic by subtype HR+ / HER2− 1L: aromatase inhibitor + CDK4/6 inhibitor progression on adjuvant ET → send NGS premenopausal: add ovarian suppression HER2+ 1L: pertuzumab + trastuzumab + taxane then T-DXd; T-DM1 brain mets: tucatinib combos (HER2CLIMB) TNBC pembrolizumab + chemo if PD-L1-positive gBRCA: olaparib or talazoparib sacituzumab govitecan; T-DXd if HER2-low Biomarker → therapy Alteration Therapy Germline BRCA1/2 Olaparib or talazoparib PD-L1-positive TNBC Pembrolizumab + chemotherapy PIK3CA Inavolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant · alpelisib · capivasertib AKT1 / PTEN Capivasertib + fulvestrant ESR1 Elacestrant HER2-low or ultralow Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) MSI-H / dMMR Pembrolizumab, dostarlimab TMB ≥10 mut/Mb Pembrolizumab NTRK fusion Larotrectinib, entrectinib, repotrectinib RET Selpercatinib Metastatic HR+/HER2− sequencing First line — de novo metastatic, or progression >12 months after endocrine therapy: aromatase inhibitor + CDK4/6 inhibitor Progression on adjuvant ET, or relapse within 12 months of it → check NGS. PIK3CA-mutant: inavolisib + palbociclib + fulvestrant. Wild-type: fulvestrant 500 mg IM d0, 14, 28 then q28d + a CDK4/6 inhibitor Progression on CDK4/6i + ET → switch CDK4/6 inhibitor — ribociclib with alternative ET (MAINTAIN) or abemaciclib + fulvestrant (postMONARCH) Endocrine-resistant: everolimus 10 mg + exemestane 25 mg daily , then chemotherapy ADCs: T-DXd if HER2-low or ultralow · sacituzumab govitecan · datopotamab deruxtecan Surgical & radiation pearls Inflammatory breast cancer: staging work-up → neoadjuvant chemotherapy → modified radical mastectomy → postoperative chest wall + regional nodal radiation — even with a pathologic complete response . Delayed reconstruction; BCS contraindicated; ALND indicated Relative contraindications to BCS radiation: Li-Fraumeni, active connective tissue disease involving skin (scleroderma, lupus), prior chest radiation, large tumor-to-breast-volume ratio Reconstruction with planned radiation: preferred is immediate tissue expander → expansion → radiation → exchange to implant, or delayed autologous Nipple-sparing mastectomy: ischemia and necrosis risk with high BMI, large or ptotic breasts, prior radiation or breast surgery Lymphedema ~5% after SLNB, highest after ALND + radiation — screen at visits; consider LYMPHA at nodal dissection; class I compression sleeve; PT referral BIA-ALCL — associated with textured implants; very rare; diagnosed on cytology; requires complete resection of capsule, implant and any mass

docs.subtitle: 2nd leading cause of cancer death · ~106,590 new cases (2024) · 5-yr survival — stage I 90%, II 70–85%, III 50–73%, IV 12–14%
docs.text: Colon adenocarcinoma 2nd leading cause of cancer death · ~106,590 new cases (2024) · 5-yr survival — stage I 90% , II 70–85% , III 50–73% , IV 12–14% Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Colon Cancer (Johnson T, Miller D) · NCCN · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter Workup Colonoscopy with biopsy + pathology review MMR / MSI testing in ALL newly diagnosed colon cancer KRAS, NRAS, BRAF mutation + HER2 amplification by NGS panel CT C/A/P · MRI liver if potentially resectable liver mets · PET/CT in selected resectable M1 Labs: CBC, CMP, CEA Genetics referral: all diagnosed <50 y , or somatic finding with germline implications BRAF V600E + MLH1 loss largely excludes Lynch — but ~1% of Lynch is BRAF V600E Staging — AJCC 8th T1 / T2 / T3 submucosa / through muscularis propria / into pericolorectal tissue T4a / T4b through visceral peritoneum / invades adjacent organ N1 / N2 1–3 nodes (N1c = deposits only) / ≥4 nodes M1a / b / c 1 site / ≥2 sites / peritoneal Stage III any node-positive, M0 Key trials IDEA 3 vs 6 mo adjuvant — failed non-inferiority overall (HR 1.07, margin 1.12), but 3 mo CAPOX non-inferior while FOLFOX favored 6 mo (Grothey, NEJM 2018) ATOMIC adding IO to adjuvant chemo in dMMR (ASCO 2025) KEYNOTE-177 1L pembrolizumab in dMMR: PFS 16.5 vs 8.2 mo BREAKWATER 1L BRAF V600E: FOLFOX + encorafenib + cetuximab BEACON BRAF V600E later line (Kopetz, NEJM 2019) Treatment pathway Localized — stage I to III Surgery first colon is resected upfront (unlike rectal) pathology drives the adjuvant decision no adjuvant therapy for stage I Stage II (node-negative) risk factors: T4, LVI, PNI, obstruction, perforation, poor differentiation, <12 nodes low risk observe; RFs 5-FU ± oxaliplatin Stage III virtually all receive adjuvant chemotherapy age <75: fluoropyrimidine + oxaliplatin age >75: fluoropyrimidine alone IDEA: 3 mo CAPOX ok — FOLFOX needs 6 mo high risk (T4 and/or N2) favors 6 months dMMR / MSI-H Immunotherapy-sensitive consider neoadjuvant IO before resection adjuvant: add IO to chemo (ATOMIC) adjuvant 5-FU alone may be HARMFUL Metastatic Oligometastatic liver/lung only: surgical consult upfront FOLFOX or CAPEOX preferred — cure possible 1L by molecular subtype dMMR: pembrolizumab (KEYNOTE-177) BRAF V600E: FOLFOX + encorafenib + cetuximab left-sided RAS/BRAF WT: doublet + anti-EGFR right-sided or RAS-mut: FOLFOXIRI ± bev Later lines stop oxaliplatin at ~4 months (neuropathy) swap backbone; HER2 matters in 2nd line Oxaliplatin neuropathy is the dominant long-term toxicity. Six months may raise the risk of permanent neuropathy as much as tenfold vs three months. Do not exceed ~4 months in initial metastatic therapy (OPTIMOX); never given as a single agent. Regimens & dosing Regimen Dosing Cycle FOLFOX oxaliplatin 85 d1 · 5-FU 1200–1500/day CIV d1–2 q14d CAPEOX / XELOX oxaliplatin 130 d1 · capecitabine 1000 BID d1–14 q21d FOLFIRI irinotecan 180 d1 · 5-FU 1200–1400/day CIV d1–2 q14d FOLFOXIRI oxaliplatin 85 · irinotecan 165 · 5-FU 1200–1400/day CIV d1–2 q14d Bevacizumab 7.5 mg/kg (q3wk) or 5 mg/kg (q2wk) q21d / q14d Cetuximab / panitumumab cetuximab 400 load then 250 weekly (or 500 q2wk) · panitumumab 6 mg/kg wkly / q2wk Regorafenib ramp 80→120→160 mg weekly in C1; then 160 mg d1–21 q28d Trifluridine/tipiracil 35 mg/m² PO BID d1–5 and d8–12 q28d Fruquintinib 5 mg PO daily × 21 days q28d All doses mg/m² unless stated. Institutional preference: no 5-FU bolus (higher toxicity) — which also removes the need for leucovorin as a stabilizer. Biomarker → therapy Alteration Therapy dMMR / MSI-H Pembrolizumab 200 mg q3wk or 400 mg q6wk — 1L metastatic; also neoadjuvant/adjuvant BRAF V600E, 1L FOLFOX + encorafenib 300 mg daily + cetuximab BRAF V600E, later Encorafenib + cetuximab; triplet adds binimetinib RAS WT + left-sided Cetuximab or panitumumab — no benefit if right-sided or RAS-mutant HER2 amplified Trastuzumab + pertuzumab; tucatinib 300 BID + trastuzumab; T-DXd NTRK fusion Larotrectinib 100 mg BID · entrectinib 600 mg daily Surveillance H&P + CEA q3–6 mo × 2 yr, then q6 mo — 5 years total CT C/A/P: stage II–III q6–12 mo × 5 yr; stage IV q3–6 mo × 2 yr then q6–12 mo Colonoscopy at 1 year post-op; within 3–6 mo if no complete pre-op scope If adenoma found repeat in 1 yr; otherwise 3 yr, then every 5 yr Pearls & cautions Irinotecan with great caution in the elderly, biliary obstruction, or hyperbilirubinemia Regorafenib is very toxic — many do better at lower doses; bevacizumab benefit is modest ctDNA timing conflict: results take 4–6 wk but adjuvant works best within 6 wk of surgery Metastatic rectal regimens are identical to metastatic CRC

docs.title: Aggressive B-cell lymphoma
docs.subtitle: DLBCL and the three situations that change the plan — Burkitt, primary CNS lymphoma, and HIV-associated disease. The recurring questions are cell of origin, double-hit status, cardiac fitness, and whether the CNS needs covering
headings: IPI — age >60 · PS ≥2 · LDH ↑ · ≥2 extranodal · stage III–IV
docs.text: Aggressive B-cell lymphoma DLBCL and the three situations that change the plan — Burkitt , primary CNS lymphoma , and HIV-associated disease. The recurring questions are cell of origin, double-hit status, cardiac fitness, and whether the CNS needs covering Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin, pp.194–222 · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter Workup Excisional lymph node biopsy preferred , core acceptable, no FNA ; hematopathology review IHC: CD20, CD10, CD30, CD5, BCL2, BCL6, MUM1, MYC, EBV + Ki-67 . Cell of origin by Hans algorithm (GCB vs non-GCB/ABC) Cytogenetics for MYC, BCL2, BCL6 — defines double/triple hit (HGBCL) Labs: CBC, CMP, LDH , uric acid, hepatitis B and C serologies, HIV PET/CT + bone marrow biopsy ; baseline echo or MUGA Situational: LP if CNS concern · endoscopy if GI concern · fertility preservation Response: PET/CT at completion, marrow biopsy if positive at diagnosis IPI — age >60 · PS ≥2 · LDH ↑ · ≥2 extranodal · stage III–IV Risk 5-yr OS pre-R 3-yr OS post-R Low (0–1) 73% 91.4% Low-intermediate (2) 51% 80.9% High-intermediate (3) 43% 65.1% High (4–5) 26% 59% Mnemonic APLES , one point each. Shipp, NEJM 1993 · Ziepert, JCO 2010. The handbook gives neither R-IPI nor NCCN-IPI. CNS risk and prophylaxis CNS-IPI IPI + kidney and/or adrenal (0–6). 2-yr CNS relapse: 0–1 = 0.6% · 2–3 = 3.4% · 4–6 = 10.2% Who gets it Mandatory: Burkitt/ALL, testicular. High risk: CNS-IPI 4–6 · double/triple hit and non-GCB · epidural, paranasal sinus or base of skull · breast or uterine Regimen Systemic HD-MTX 3–3.5 g/m² ×2–4 after completing systemic therapy — preferred in fit patients with adequate renal function for parenchymal penetration. Or IT MTX ± cytarabine ×4–8 The handbook calls the benefit controversial (Wilson, Blood 2022) — consider in selected high-risk patients, not routinely. Treatment pathway Frontline Limited stage I–II R-CHOP ×3 + ISRT 30–36 Gy (SWOG 8736), or R-CHOP ×4 (FLYER) — ×6 if bulky SWOG 8736 was pre-rituximab; its advantage was lost on long follow-up Advanced: II smIPI 2+, or III–IV R-CHOP ×6 or Pola-R-CHP ×6 + 2 rituximab DA-EPOCH-R instead if double hit or PMBCL Cardiac dysfunction Anthracycline-sparing DA-EPOCH-R + dexrazoxane · R-CDOP R-CEPP · R-CEOP · R-GCVP borderline: R-CHOP + dexrazoxane + TTE Second line Relapse <1 yr or transplant-ineligible CAR-T is standard — axi-cel or liso-cel bridge: R-DHAP/DHAX, R-GemOx, Pola-R-GemOx, R-ICE neither CAR-T nor ASCT: bispecific + GemOx, Pola-BR, or tafasitamab + lenalidomide Third line and beyond Trial first CAR-T if not already given bispecifics: ≥2 lines AND post-cellular therapy loncastuximab · selinexor · R² Recurring supportive care. Antiviral + PJP prophylaxis with nearly every regimen: acyclovir 400 mg BID + Bactrim DS three times weekly (or SS daily). G-CSF with R-CHOP if age ≥60, required with Pola-R-CHP. Cytarabine → prednisolone 1% eye drops 2 gtt OU BID from 12 h before until 48 h after; reduce cytarabine to 1 g/m² if age >60. Mesna with every ifosfamide. Frontline regimens Regimen Dosing Cycle R-CHOP Rituximab 375 · cyclophosphamide 750 · doxorubicin 50 · vincristine 1.4 (max 2 mg) all d1; prednisone 40/day PO d1–5 q21d ×6 Pola-R-CHP Polatuzumab vedotin 1.8 mg/kg · rituximab 375 · cyclophosphamide 750 · doxorubicin 50 all d1; prednisone 100 mg PO d1–5 q21d ×6, +2 rituximab DA-EPOCH-R Rituximab 375 d1; doxorubicin 10/day + etoposide 50/day + vincristine 0.4/day (max 2 mg) all CIV d1–4; cyclophosphamide 750 d5; prednisone 60/day PO d1–5 q21d ×6 R-CEOP Cyclophosphamide 750 + vincristine 1.4 d1; etoposide 50 IV d1 then 100 PO d2–3; prednisone 40/day d1–5 q21d ×4–6 R-CEPP Cyclophosphamide 600 d1; etoposide 70 d1–3; prednisone 60 + procarbazine 60 PO d1–10 q28d ×6 R-GCVP Gemcitabine 1000 d1+8; cyclophosphamide 750 + vincristine 1–1.4 d1; prednisolone 100 mg PO d1–5 q21d All mg/m² unless stated. DA-EPOCH-R escalation (etoposide, doxorubicin, cyclophosphamide; CBC twice weekly): ANC nadir ≥500 throughout → +20% ; <500 on 1–2 checks → same; <500 on 3 checks or platelets <25k → −20% . Salvage and later-line Regimen Dosing Cycle R-ICE Ifosfamide 5000 + mesna 5000 CIV d2; carboplatin AUC 5 (max 800 mg) d2; etoposide 100 d1–3 q14–21d R-DHAP · R-DHAX Cytarabine 2000 q12h ×2 d2 + dexamethasone 40 mg d1–4, with cisplatin 100 (DHAP) or oxaliplatin 100 (DHAX) d1 q21–28d R-ESHAP Methylprednisolone 500 mg d1–5; etoposide 40 d1–4; cisplatin 25/day CIV d1–4; cytarabine 2000 d5 q21–28d R-GDP · R-GCD Gemcitabine 1000 d1+8; dexamethasone 40 mg PO d1–4; cisplatin 75 d1 (GDP) or carboplatin AUC 5 (GCD) q21d R-GemOx Gemcitabine 1000 + oxaliplatin 100 d1 q14–21d ×6 Pola-BR Polatuzumab 1.8 mg/kg + rituximab 375 d1; bendamustine 90 d1+2 q21d ×6 Tafasitamab + len Tafasitamab 12 mg/kg d1; lenalidomide 25 mg PO d1–21 q28d ×12 Epcoritamab SQ step-up: 0.16 mg C1D1 → 0.8 mg C1D8 → 48 mg C1D15 , then weekly to C3, q2wk C4–9, q4wk C10+ q28d Glofitamab Obinutuzumab 1000 mg C1D1 pretreatment, then 2.5 mg C1D8 → 10 mg C1D15 → 30 mg C2D1 q21d ×12 Transplant candidates get 2–3 cycles of platinum salvage; non-transplant 4–6. Cytarabine → 1 g/m² if age >60. Either bispecific may be given with GemOx. Pearls DA-EPOCH-R, not R-CHOP, for double-hit HGBCL and primary mediastinal B-cell lymphoma R-CEOP outcomes appear inferior to R-CHOP (Puckrin 2022) — for borderline cardiomyopathy prefer R-CHOP + dexrazoxane with echo surveillance over switching regimen CAR-T now precedes transplant in second line for early relapse — platinum salvage is bridging, not destination therapy No MTX with effusions or ascites , or with PPIs, penicillins, TMP-SMX, salicylates, probenecid or NSAIDs Staging — Cotswolds-modified Ann Arbor I One lymph node region or lymphoid structure (spleen, thymus, Waldeyer ring) II ≥2 regions, same side of the diaphragm. Hilar nodes are lateralized — bilateral involvement is stage II III Regions on both sides of the diaphragm IV Disseminated — marrow, CNS, or more than one extranodal site A / B B = weight loss >10% over 6 mo, or unexplained fever >38°C in the past month, or recurrent drenching night sweats S · X · E S splenic · X bulky: node ≥10 cm , or mediastinal mass ≥⅓ the transverse thoracic diameter at T5–6 · E limited direct extranodal extension A single extranodal site as the only disease is IE; more than one extranodal site is stage IV. Hilar (bronchopulmonary) nodes sit outside the mediastinum. Burkitt — risk and parameters Low risk ALL of: normal LDH, ECOG 0–1, stage I–II, no mass ≥10 cm, ≤1 extranodal site High risk Everything else Baseline HIV, HBsAg, HBcAb, HBsAb, HCV Ab · echocardiogram for EF To start a cycle ANC >1000, platelets >75,000, direct bili <1.4, Cr <1.2 — does not apply to cycle 1, nor to the day-10 HD-MTX, which is given regardless of counts Also staged by St. Jude/Murphy. Every Burkitt patient gets CNS prophylaxis. Burkitt pathway Modified Magrath Low risk R-CODOX-M ×3 (A-A-A), q3wk High risk, CNS negative A-B-A-B ×4 — R-CODOX-M / R-IVAC High risk, CNS positive A-B-A-B ×4 + extra IT each cycle 16 intrathecal treatments total Alternatives Listed in the chapter R-hyperCVAD, alternating A/B ×6–8 DA-EPOCH-R : low risk ×3 no IT; high risk ×6 with IT CALGB 10002 Burkitt TLS (cycle 1). Allopurinol 300 mg BID · labs q8h (K, Phos, Ca, Cr, LDH, uric acid) · NS 2 L/m²/day · strict I/O with goal output 100 mL/h — continue ≥72 h after chemotherapy . Rasburicase 6 mg IV ×1 for WBC ≥100,000, uric acid >7.5, or renal dysfunction; contraindicated in G6PD deficiency ; the confirmatory uric acid at 4 h must go in a pre-chilled heparin tube on ice . No LP if circulating blasts or platelets <50,000. Modified Magrath (Mead, Blood 2008) Cycle Dosing A — R-CODOX-M Rituximab 375 d1 · cyclophosphamide 800 d1 + 200 d2–5 (first A cycle; later A cycles 800 d1+2) · doxorubicin 40 d1 · vincristine 1.5 (cap 2 mg) d1+8 · MTX 3000 total over 24 h on d10 (300 over 1 h, then 2700 over 23 h) · IT cytarabine 70 mg d1+3 · IT MTX 12 mg d15 B — R-IVAC Rituximab 375 d1 · etoposide 60 d1–5 · ifosfamide 1500 d1–5 + mesna · cytarabine 2000 q12h ×4 doses d1–2 · IT MTX 12 mg d5 Age >65 MTX 1000 total (100 over 1 h, then 900 over 23 h) · ifosfamide 1000 · cytarabine 1000 If CNS positive Add IT cytarabine 70 mg d5 and IT MTX 12 mg d17 (cycle A); IT cytarabine 70 mg d7 and d9 (cycle B) Leucovorin 15 mg PO 24 h after each IT MTX. Start G-CSF only after the MTX level is <0.02. High-dose MTX administration Before starting Hydrate/alkalinize: ½NS + 100 mEq NaHCO₃ at 500 mL/h ×2 h then 125 mL/h. Do not start until urine pH >7 and output >100 mL/h Do not give if Pleural effusion, ascites or any fluid collection — or concurrently with PPIs, penicillins, TMP-SMX, salicylates, probenecid, NSAIDs Renal dosing 50% if CrCl 10–50 ; omit if <10; 25–50% for prior delayed excretion, nephrotoxicity or grade III–IV mucositis Leucovorin rescue 25 mg IV q6h ×4 starting 36 h after the START of MTX , then 25 mg PO q6h until level <0.02 Escalate rescue 24 h: Cr up >50% or level >20 µM · 48 h: level >1 µM · 72 h: level >0.1 µM → leucovorin 100 mg/m² IV q6h Keep urine pH >7 until the level clears; check levels q24h. Glucarpidase is not mentioned in the chapter. Trials the chapter cites Trial Supports FLYER (Poeschel, Lancet 2019) R-CHOP ×4 for favorable limited stage POLARIX (Tilly, NEJM 2022) Pola-R-CHP vs R-CHOP frontline L-MIND (Salles, Lancet Oncol 2020) Tafasitamab + lenalidomide, ASCT-ineligible Thieblemont JCO 2023 · Dickinson NEJM 2022 Epcoritamab and glofitamab monotherapy Roschewski, JCO 2020 Risk-adapted DA-EPOCH-R in Burkitt CALGB 50202 (Rubenstein, JCO 2013) MT-R induction + EA consolidation in PCNSL IELSG32 / MATRIX (Ferreri, Lancet Haem 2016) MTX/cytarabine/thiotepa/rituximab Schmitz, JCO 2016 CNS-IPI The handbook cites by author with no acronyms or results. Names, numbers and endpoints were verified against the primary publications — full cards on the Hub. PCNSL IELSG index 1 point each: age >60 · PS >1 · elevated LDH · high CSF protein · deep brain involvement . 2-yr OS 0–1: 80% · 2–3: 48% · 4–5: 15% MSKCC model <50 yr: median OS 5.2 yr · ≥50 + KPS ≥70: 2.1 yr · ≥50 + KPS <70: 0.8 yr Induction Trial, or an HD-MTX backbone : MT-R (CALGB 50202) · R-MPV · HD-MTX alone · R-MTX-AraC · MATRIX . MTX-ineligible: rituximab + temozolomide MT-R MTX 8000 over 4 h d1; rituximab 375 d3 (first 6 doses); temozolomide 150 PO d7–11 every other cycle. q14d ×8 R-MPV Rituximab 500 (not 375) · MTX 3500 over 4 h · vincristine 1.4 (max 2.8 mg) d1 · procarbazine 100 PO d1–7 odd cycles. q14d ×5 MATRIX Rituximab 375 d−5 and d0 · MTX 3500 d1 · cytarabine 2000 q12h ×4 d2–3 · thiotepa 30 d4 . q21d Consolidation CR → HD therapy + stem-cell rescue · cytarabine 3000 d1+2 monthly ×2 ± etoposide · lenalidomide 15 mg or BTKi maintenance R-MPV → WBRT CR → 23.4 Gy ; PR → 2 more cycles then 23.4 Gy if CR, 45 Gy if persistent; SD/PD → 45 Gy Relapse Trial · HD cytarabine ± etoposide · CAR-T · lenalidomide · BTKi · WBRT · best supportive care Leucovorin starts 24 h after the MTX start in PCNSL protocols, vs 36 h in the Burkitt guidelines above. PCP prophylaxis TMP-SMX DS BID Sat/Sun throughout. The chapter's workup sits in a figure that did not survive text extraction — biopsy, steroid timing, slit-lamp and CSF are not in the text. HIV-associated lymphoma Also in immunocompetent Burkitt · DLBCL · PCNSL · MALT · peripheral T-cell · classical Hodgkin More specific to HIV Primary effusion lymphoma · plasmablastic lymphoma Other immunodeficiency Polymorphic B-cell lymphoma (PTLD-like) Treatment R-CHOP q21d ×4–6 · DA-EPOCH-R q21d ×6 · modified Magrath (see Burkitt). The chapter does not map regimen to category Antiretrovirals Continue HAART through chemotherapy, or start it if not already on treatment. No interaction table is given CNS prophylaxis For small non-cleaved histology, or marrow, paranasal sinus, testicular or epidural involvement — IT MTX 12 mg d1+5 of cycles 3–5 (6 doses), or weekly IT ×4 during cycle 1 Prophylaxis PCP TMP-SMX DS BID Sat/Sun · MAC azithromycin 1200 mg weekly if CD4 <100 · fluconazole 100 mg daily · acyclovir 400 mg BID No CD4 threshold for withholding rituximab appears anywhere in the chapter — CD4 <100 is cited only as the trigger for MAC and quinolone prophylaxis. † Deauville 5-point score 1 · 2 No uptake · uptake ≤ mediastinum 3 Uptake > mediastinum but ≤ liver — usually adequate response 4 · 5 Moderately > liver · markedly > liver or new lesions — treatment failure † Not in the handbook chapter, which specifies only PET/CT at completion (plus marrow biopsy if positive at diagnosis). Added because response is reported this way in practice and in every trial cited here.

docs.title: Hodgkin lymphoma
docs.subtitle: Highly curable, and managed by interim PET more than by anything else — the whole game is giving enough therapy to cure while withdrawing bleomycin and radiation from the people who don't need them
docs.text: Hodgkin lymphoma Highly curable, and managed by interim PET more than by anything else — the whole game is giving enough therapy to cure while withdrawing bleomycin and radiation from the people who don't need them Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Hodgkin, pp.181–192 (Chou L, Schroers-Martin J) · NCCN v2.2025 · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter Workup History: B symptoms, pruritus, alcohol intolerance ; exam of nodal regions, liver, spleen. Marrow biopsy only for focal bone lesions or unexplained cytopenias Excisional biopsy preferred , core acceptable, no FNA IHC — most critical: CD30, CD15, PAX5, CD20, CD3 Labs: CBC, CMP, ESR , LDH, HIV, hepatitis B and C PET-CT for staging Echo/MUGA before anthracycline · PFTs before bleomycin · before a checkpoint inhibitor: TSH, ACTH, cortisol, troponin Fertility discussion — risk is low with A(B)VD , so preservation is not mandated frontline; bank before salvage Staging — Cotswolds-modified Ann Arbor I One lymph node region or lymphoid structure (spleen, thymus, Waldeyer ring) II ≥2 regions, same side of the diaphragm. Hilar nodes are lateralized — bilateral involvement is stage II III Regions on both sides of the diaphragm IV Disseminated — marrow, CNS, or more than one extranodal site A / B B = weight loss >10% over 6 mo, or unexplained fever >38°C in the past month, or recurrent drenching night sweats S · X · E S splenic · X bulky: node ≥10 cm , or mediastinal mass ≥⅓ the transverse thoracic diameter at T5–6 · E limited direct extranodal extension A single extranodal site as the only disease is IE; more than one extranodal site is stage IV. Hilar (bronchopulmonary) nodes sit outside the mediastinum. Early-stage risk factors Factor EORTC GHSG NCCN Mediastinal mass >0.35 CXR >⅓ CXR >⅓ or >10 cm Age ≥50 yes — — ESR ≥50 (≥30 if B) ≥50 (≥30 if B) ≥50 or any B Extranodal disease — yes — Nodal areas ≥3 ≥2 ≥3 Favorable = CS I–II with none of these. GHSG counts nodal areas differently from Ann Arbor (infraclavicular with ipsilateral cervical, both hila with mediastinum, abdomen split in two). IPS — advanced stage Factors FFP Hasenclever FFP Moccia 0–1 84–77% 88–84% 2–3 67–60% 80–74% ≥4 51–42% 67–62% One point each: albumin <4 · Hgb <10.5 · male · stage IV · age ≥45 · WBC ≥15,000 · lymphocytes <600 or <8% . Hasenclever NEJM 1998; Moccia JCO 2012 is the modern-era revision. Treatment pathway Early favorable (CS I–II, no risk factors) PET-adapted, two routes GHSG-favorable: ABVD ×2 → 20 Gy ISRT (HD16) otherwise ABVD ×3 → 30 Gy if DS 1–2 chemo only: ABVD ×4 if DS 1–2 DS 3 → ABVD ×2 then AVD ×4 (RATHL) Early unfavorable Combined modality or chemo alone ABVD ×4 + 30 Gy ISRT if DS 1–2 nivo-AVD ×4 + 30 Gy (NIVAHL) · BV-AVD (BREACH) chemo only: ABVD ×2 → AVD ×4 — drop bleomycin after cycle 2 if DS 1–3 (RATHL) Advanced III–IV Two modern standards BrECADD ×4–6 (HD21) — stop at 4 if DS 1–3 nivolumab-AVD ×6 (S1826) selected: BV-AVD ×6 (ECHELON-1), ABVD Relapsed / refractory Checkpoint combo is preferred first salvage pembro-GVD · pembro-ICE · nivo-ICE · BV-nivo non-CPI: BeGEV, BV ± benda, BV-ICE, DHAP, GVD, ICE 2–4 cycles then mobilize if transplant-bound NLPHL A different disease I–IIA contiguous non-bulky: ISRT 30–36 Gy I–IIB or bulky: R-ABVD/R-CHOP ×4 + 30 Gy III–IV: R-CHOP ×6 ± ISRT, or observe transformation to THRLBCL → treat as DLBCL † Deauville 5-point score 1 · 2 No uptake · uptake ≤ mediastinum 3 Uptake > mediastinum but ≤ liver — usually adequate response 4 · 5 Moderately > liver · markedly > liver or new lesions — treatment failure † Not in the handbook chapter, which specifies only PET/CT at completion (plus marrow biopsy if positive at diagnosis). Added because response is reported this way in practice and in every trial cited here. Frontline regimens Regimen Dosing Cycle ABVD Doxorubicin 25 · bleomycin 10 units/m² · vinblastine 6 · dacarbazine 375 — all d1 + d15 q28d Nivolumab-AVD Nivolumab 240 mg · doxorubicin 25 · vinblastine 6 · dacarbazine 375 — all d1 + d15. G-CSF not required d1 + d15 BrECADD Brentuximab 1.8 d0 · etoposide 150 d1–3 · cyclophosphamide 1250 d1 · doxorubicin 40 d1 · vincristine 1.4 d8 · dacarbazine 250 d2–3 · dexamethasone 40 mg d1–4 q21d with G-CSF BV-AVD Brentuximab 1.2 mg/kg · doxorubicin 25 · vinblastine 6 · dacarbazine 375 — all d1 + d15; filgrastim d5–8 and d19–22 q28d mg/m² unless stated. BrECADD starts at dose level 4 and de-escalates for toxicity. Antiviral + PJP prophylaxis with every brentuximab-containing regimen. Salvage regimens Regimen Dosing Cycle Pembro-GVD Pembrolizumab 200 mg d1; gemcitabine 1000 (800 if post-HSCT) + vinorelbine 15 + liposomal doxorubicin 10 — all d1 + d8 q21d ×2–4 Pembro-ICE · nivo-ICE Checkpoint inhibitor d1 + ICE: ifosfamide 5000 + mesna 5000 CIV d2; carboplatin AUC 5 (max 800 mg) d2; etoposide 100 d1–3 q21d ×2, then collect BV + nivolumab Brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg (max 180 mg) d1; nivolumab 240 mg C1D8 then d1 of C2–4 q21d ×4 BV ± benda · BeGEV Brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg d1 ± bendamustine 90 d1–2 (BV alone ×16 cycles) · BeGEV = gemcitabine 800 d1+4, bendamustine 90 d2+3, vinorelbine 20 d1, prednisolone 100 mg d1–4 q21d GVD · ICE · DHAP Gemcitabine/vinorelbine/liposomal doxorubicin · ifosfamide-carbo-etoposide · cisplatin + cytarabine 2000 q12h ×2 + dexamethasone q21–28d 2–4 cycles then mobilization for transplant candidates, 4–6 otherwise. Checkpoint monotherapy responds often but completes rarely — combine it. Pearls Do not give G-CSF with ABVD — bleomycin pulmonary toxicity. Do not delay or dose-reduce for non-febrile neutropenia; if unavoidable (ANC <200 or febrile neutropenia) give it day 5 or later ×3–5 days Bilateral hilar involvement is stage II , not III — hilar nodes are lateralized, and they sit outside the mediastinum In relapse, give a checkpoint combination first if the patient is CPI-naive — post-ASCT outcomes are better † The handbook defers survivorship to NCCN — cardiac late effects, second malignancy and post-chest-RT breast screening are not in it Trials behind the pathway Trial Role HD16 ABVD ×2 + 20 Gy for GHSG-favorable early stage with a negative interim PET RAPID · EORTC H10 PET-adapted radiation omission vs combined modality in early stage RATHL Drop bleomycin after 2 cycles if interim PET is negative HD21 BrECADD vs eBEACOPP in advanced stage — the current European standard SWOG S1826 Nivolumab-AVD vs BV-AVD in advanced stage KEYNOTE-204 Pembrolizumab vs brentuximab, relapsed HD16, RAPID and H10 all failed non-inferiority — omitting RT costs ~4–7% PFS, though OS is unchanged.

docs.title: Indolent and mantle B-cell lymphoma
docs.subtitle: Follicular and mantle cell — grouped because both are managed as chronic disease with BTK inhibitors, bendamustine and maintenance, not because mantle cell is indolent. It is not: it is biologically aggressive and behaves like a disease you manage rather than cure
docs.text: Indolent and mantle B-cell lymphoma Follicular and mantle cell — grouped because both are managed as chronic disease with BTK inhibitors, bendamustine and maintenance, not because mantle cell is indolent. It is not : it is biologically aggressive and behaves like a disease you manage rather than cure Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin, pp.223–232 · NCCN B-Cell Lymphoma v2.2025 · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter Follicular grade Grade Incidence Histology and behavior I 40–45% 0–5 centroblasts/hpf — indolent, “classic FL” (WHO 2022) II 30% 6–15 centroblasts/hpf — indolent, classic FL IIIa 20% >15 centroblasts/hpf, centrocytes present — indolent or aggressive IIIb — >15 centroblasts/hpf, centrocytes absent , sheets of centroblasts — aggressive, behaves like DLBCL FLIPI — “NoLASH”, 1 point each Risk % 5-yr OS 10-yr OS Low (0–1) 36 91% 71% Intermediate (2) 37 78% 51% High (3–5) 27 53% 36% No dal sites >4 · L DH elevated · A ge ≥60 · S tage III–IV · H gb <12. FLIPI2 instead uses age >60, β2-microglobulin > ULN, marrow involvement, Hgb <12 and largest node >6 cm — 5-yr PFS 80% / 51% / 19% . GELF — when to treat follicular • ≥3 nodal areas each ≥3 cm • Any nodal or extranodal mass ≥7 cm • Symptoms attributable to disease, including B symptoms or effusions/ascites • Cytopenias from lymphoma (WBC <1,000 and/or platelets <100,000) • Leukemic phase >5,000 cells/µL • Splenomegaly Meeting none of these is a reason to observe , not to treat. Brice, JCO 1997 · NCCN v2.2025. MIPI — mantle cell Points Age ECOG LDH / ULN WBC K/uL 0 <50 0–1 <0.67 <6.7 1 50–59 — 0.67–0.99 6.7–9.99 2 60–69 2–4 1.00–1.49 10–14.99 3 ≥70 — ≥1.50 ≥15 Hoster, Blood 2008. The handbook prints the points table but not the risk-group cutoffs or their survival . TP53 in mantle cell. Mutated in ~10% and a strong predictor of poor outcome with chemotherapy and with autologous transplant, and also with ibrutinib. Send NGS at diagnosis ; prefer a clinical trial. Deep responses have been seen with targeted combinations — BOVen (zanubrutinib/obinutuzumab/venetoclax) and OAsIs. Follicular pathway First line Low burden — no GELF criteria observe , or rituximab weekly ×4 High burden bendamustine, CHOP or CVP + rituximab or obinutuzumab · or R² older/unfit: rituximab ± chlorambucil Maintenance and beyond Maintenance, then relapse rituximab q8–12 wk ×2 yr (PRIMA) — optional; prolongs time to next treatment, no OS benefit Second and third line 2L: any DLBCL second-line option ; auto-HCT 3L: bispecifics (epcoritamab, mosunetuzumab) CAR-T (axi-cel, liso-cel, tisa-cel) tazemetostat · zanubrutinib + obinutuzumab Mantle cell pathway Induction Fit, TP53 wild-type TRIANGLE : alternating R-CHOP + ibrutinib / R-DHAP Nordic (maxi-CHOP / R + HiDAC) → auto-HCT LyMA · R-hyperCVAD · RBAC Lower intensity, elderly or unfit acalabrutinib + bendamustine + rituximab BR · VR-CAP · R-CHOP · R² TP53 mutant zanubrutinib/obinutuzumab/venetoclax (BOVen) or the TRIANGLE regimen — trial preferred Maintenance and relapse Maintenance after high intensity: BTKi ×2 yr + rituximab q8wk ×2–3 yr after lower intensity: rituximab q8wk ×3 yr Relapsed 2L: BTKi — acalabrutinib or zanubrutinib after BTKi: CAR-T (brexu-cel, liso-cel) or pirtobrutinib (non-covalent BTKi) The case for autologous transplant in mantle cell has collapsed. The old PFS benefit predates BTKi and maintenance. TRIANGLE found no benefit once ibrutinib was added, and EA4151 none for patients in MRD-negative CR . Regimens Regimen Dosing Cycle Rituximab alone 375 d1, 8, 15, 22 single course R-bendamustine Rituximab 375 d1; bendamustine 90 d1+2 q28d ×6 R-CHOP · R-CVP Rituximab 375 · cyclophosphamide 750 · vincristine 1.4 (max 2 mg) d1 + prednisone 40/day d1–5, with doxorubicin 50 (CHOP) or without (CVP) q21d ×6–8 Maintenance rituximab 375 q2 months ×2 years (PRIMA). In MCL: 375 weekly ×4 q6 mo ×2 yr, or q3 mo ×2 yr — Obinutuzumab 1000 mg d1, 8, 15, then monthly C2–6/8, then bimonthly ×2 yr — R² Rituximab 375 d1; lenalidomide 20 mg PO d1–21 + ASA 81 mg q28d ×12 R-GemOx Rituximab 375 · gemcitabine 1000 · oxaliplatin 100, all d1 q14d ×6–8 PEP-C (palliative, oral) Prednisone 20 + cyclophosphamide 50 + etoposide 50 + procarbazine 50 mg, all PO daily until WBC <3,000, then resume on a reduced schedule continuous Mod. R-hyperCVAD Rituximab 375 d1; cyclophosphamide 300 q12h d1–3 (6 doses); doxorubicin 25 CIV d1+2; vincristine 2 mg d3; dexamethasone 40 mg d1–4 q28d ×6, then maintenance R R-DHAP Rituximab 375 d1; cisplatin 100 CIV d1; cytarabine 2000 q12h ×2 d2; dexamethasone 40 mg d1–4 q21d ×3 VR-CAP Bortezomib 1.3 SQ d2, 5, 9, 12; rituximab 375 + cyclophosphamide 1000 d1; prednisone 100 mg d2–6 q21d ×8 BTK inhibitors Ibrutinib 560 mg daily · acalabrutinib 100 mg BID · zanubrutinib 160 mg BID (or 320 mg daily) — continuous until progression continuous mg/m² unless stated. Cytarabine → 1 g/m² if age >60 , with prednisolone 1% eye drops. R-GemOx needs ANC ≥1,000 and platelets ≥100,000 to proceed. Consider aspirin with lenalidomide. Pearls Follicular grade IIIb is not an indolent lymphoma — centrocytes are absent and it is treated as DLBCL Maintenance rituximab buys time to next treatment, not survival — worth saying out loud when consenting Mantle cell TP53 mutation changes the plan , not just the prognosis — chemotherapy, transplant and ibrutinib all underperform; go to trial or a targeted combination † The handbook covers no mantle cell biology — cyclin D1, t(11;14), SOX11, Ki-67 and the blastoid variant are absent , as is the indolent leukemic-non-nodal subset that can be observed Trials Trial Role PRIMA Maintenance rituximab ×2 yr after frontline immunochemotherapy in follicular StiL NHL1 BR vs R-CHOP — the basis for BR frontline GALLIUM Obinutuzumab vs rituximab with chemotherapy in follicular RELEVANCE R² vs R-chemo — negative superiority trial ; R² is equivalent TRIANGLE Ibrutinib in induction + maintenance — no benefit from auto-HCT (endpoint: FFS) ECOG-ACRIN EA4151 No auto-HCT benefit in MRD-negative complete remission SHINE · ECHO BTK inhibitor added to chemoimmunotherapy in older MCL Numbers on the Hub cards come from the primary publications — the handbook prints citations without results.

docs.title: T-cell and cutaneous lymphoma
docs.subtitle: Outcomes well behind B-cell disease — PTCL is consolidated with transplant in first remission, while mycosis fungoides is managed for decades. CD30 and blood involvement are the findings that change the plan
docs.text: T-cell and cutaneous lymphoma Outcomes well behind B-cell disease — PTCL is consolidated with transplant in first remission , while mycosis fungoides is managed for decades . CD30 and blood involvement are the findings that change the plan Stanford Oncology Handbook 2025, Lymphoma: Non-Hodgkin, pp.233–246 · NCCN Primary Cutaneous Lymphoma v2.2025 · items marked † are outside the handbook chapter Where T/NK neoplasms live Nodal PTCL-NOS · AITL and nodal TFH lymphomas · ALCL, ALK+ or ALK− (DUSP22 / TP63 / NOS) · EBV+ nodal T-cell Extranodal Extranodal NK/T, nasal type · enteropathy-associated (EATL) · monomorphic epitheliotropic intestinal (MEITL) · hepatosplenic · subcutaneous panniculitis-like Cutaneous Mycosis fungoides · primary cutaneous CD30+ LPDs (lymphomatoid papulosis, C-ALCL) · primary cutaneous gamma/delta Leukemic Sezary syndrome · ATLL · T-PLL · T-LGL · aggressive NK-cell leukemia WHO 5th edition 2024. Sezary syndrome sits in both the cutaneous and leukemic columns — that duality is the point: it is mycosis fungoides with blood involvement. PIT — peripheral T-cell lymphoma Factors 5-yr OS 10-yr OS 0 62.3% 54.9% 1 52.9% 38.8% 2 32.9% 18.0% 3–4 18.3% 12.6% One point each: age >60 · LDH > normal · ECOG 2–4 · marrow involvement . Gallamini, Blood 2004. Staging otherwise uses Ann Arbor. Compare these numbers with aggressive B-cell disease — even no-risk-factor PTCL does worse than high-risk DLBCL. MF/SS — ISCL/EORTC TNMB T1 · T2 Patches/plaques <10% BSA · >10% BSA (T2a patch only, T2b plaque) T3 · T4 One or more tumors >1 cm · erythroderma ≥80% BSA N1–N3 Clinically abnormal nodes by Dutch grade 1 / 2 / 3–4 (NCI LN 0–2 / 3 / 4) B0 ≤5% of lymphocytes are Sezary cells, or <250/µL, and <15% CD4+CD26− or CD4+CD7− B1 >5% Sezary cells or >15% CD4+CD26−/CD7−, but not B2 B2 >1,000/µL Sezary cells or >1,000 CD4+CD26−/CD7− cells/µL with a blood clone matching the skin Stage IA T1 · IB T2 · IIA T1–2 N1–2 · IIB T3 · IIIA/B T4 with B0/B1 · IVA1 = Sezary syndrome (any T, B2) · IVA2 N3 · IVB M1. Olsen, Blood 2022. Pearls Auto-HCT in first remission is the default for PTCL — the exception is ALCL with an ALK or DUSP22 rearrangement, which does well without it Allogeneic transplant is potentially curative in advanced MF/SS — 1-yr and 3-yr OS 51% and 40%, PFS 42% and 33%, with acute and chronic GVHD 45% and 40% † Sezary syndrome requires all three: erythroderma (T4, ≥80% BSA), B2 blood burden, and a T-cell clone in blood matching the skin . The older ISCL adjuncts — CD4:CD8 ≥10 and loss of CD7 or CD26 — no longer stand alone; modified ISCL/USCLC/EORTC criteria need the clone plus an absolute count. The handbook prints none of this, giving only stage IVA1 Treatment pathway PTCL frontline Subtype and CD30 drive the choice ALCL: BV-CHP preferred PTCL-NOS, AITL, TFH: BV-CHP if CD30+ , else CHOP / CHOEP / DA-EPOCH · EATL: IVE/MTX then auto-HCT if transplant-eligible — except ALCL with ALK or DUSP22 rearrangement PTCL relapsed Single agents, then combinations belinostat · romidepsin · pralatrexate · duvelisib BV if CD30+ · gemcitabine · bendamustine ALK+ ALCL: an ALK inhibitor (alectinib, crizotinib...) combos: DHAP · ESHAP · GDP · GVD · GemOx · ICE NK/T-cell, nasal type Asparaginase + radiation DEVIC q21d ×3 + concurrent RT 50 Gy , or modified SMILE q28d ×2–6 Mycosis fungoides / Sezary Stage IA–IIB IA–IIA: skin-directed therapy , alone or combined IIB: local RT if limited, TSEBT if generalized, ± systemic Erythrodermic III, Sezary IV, and LCT <5K/mm³ : ECP + interferon or retinoids, TSEBT + ECP >5K/mm³ : mogamulizumab, romidepsin, alemtuzumab LCT : BV, gemcitabine, liposomal doxorubicin, pralatrexate, romidepsin, mogamulizumab PTCL and NK/T regimens Regimen Dosing Cycle Pralatrexate 30 mg/m² IV weekly ×6 — folic acid 1–1.25 mg daily from 7–10 d before until 30 d after, B12 1 mg IM q8–10 wk q7 wk Romidepsin · belinostat Romidepsin 14 mg/m² over 4 h d1, 8, 15 q28d ×6 · belinostat 1,000 mg/m² over 30 min d1–5 q21d ×8 — Duvelisib 75 mg PO BID ×2 cycles, then 25 mg PO BID q28d, continuous Gemcitabine · brentuximab Gemcitabine 1,200 mg/m² d1, 8, 15 q28d · brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg d1 (max 180 mg) q21d ×16 if CD30+ — DEVIC Dexamethasone 40 mg + ifosfamide 1,000 + mesna + etoposide 67, all d1–3; carboplatin 200 d1 q21d ×3 + RT 50 Gy Modified SMILE MTX 2,000 d1 · ifosfamide 1,500 + mesna + dexamethasone 40 mg + etoposide 100 d2–4 · pegaspargase 2,000 U/m² d7 , hold until MTX <0.04. Leucovorin from 24 h. TMP-SMX DS BID Sat/Sun q28d ×2–6 CHOP/CHOEP/BV-CHP/DA-EPOCH dosing is not in this chapter — see the aggressive B-cell card. EATL : CHOP ×1 then IVE (ifosfamide 3,000 + etoposide 200 d1–3, epirubicin 50 d1) alternating with MTX 1,500 d22, q28d ×3, then auto-HCT. MF/SS therapies Therapy Dosing and notes Skin-directed Topical corticosteroids · imiquimod · mechlorethamine (often compounded) · topical retinoids · local ISRT 8–12 Gy (24–30 Gy if unilesional) · TSEBT 12–36 Gy · PUVA for thicker plaques, NB-UVB for thinner Bexarotene 300 mg/m² PO daily — causes central hypothyroidism: follow free T4, not TSH ; check lipids. Vorinostat 400 mg PO daily · IFN alfa-2a 3–6 MU daily or TIW · ECP Mogamulizumab 1 mg/kg IV d1, 8, 15, 22 then q28d — CCR4 antibody, best in Sezary/blood disease . Mogamulizumab-associated rash is delayed, median onset 119 days Romidepsin · brentuximab Romidepsin 14 mg/m² d1, 8, 15 q28d — QTc prolongation, replete Mg each infusion . Brentuximab 1.8 mg/kg q3wk — thicker skin disease and LCT only ; watch neuropathy Methotrexate → pralatrexate MTX 25 mg PO weekly (start 10–15, titrate); if higher doses are needed switch to pralatrexate 15 mg/m² d1, 8, 15 q28d — half the PTCL dose ; mucositis is dose-limiting Alemtuzumab 3 mg d1 then 10 mg SQ on alternating days, TIW, max 12 wk — stage III/T4 or Sezary only ; CMV PCR q2–3 wk , Bactrim + acyclovir Pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3wk — continue indefinitely; stopping can lose the response Maximise skin-directed therapy and supportive care first — it lengthens time to the next systemic treatment. Check compatibility with TSEBT/phototherapy first, and recycle agents that previously worked. Trials Trial Role ECHELON-2 BV-CHP vs CHOP in CD30+ PTCL — the reason ALCL gets brentuximab frontline PROPEL Pralatrexate in relapsed PTCL BELIEF Belinostat in relapsed/refractory PTCL ALCANZA Brentuximab vs physician's choice in CD30+ CTCL MAVORIC Mogamulizumab vs vorinostat in MF/SS — the registrational trial Yamaguchi JCO 2009 DEVIC + concurrent RT in NK/T nasal type

docs.title: Myelodysplastic syndromes
docs.subtitle: Clonal stem-cell disorders with ineffective hematopoiesis → cytopenias, dysplasia, and variable AML risk · blasts <20% · everything collapses to lower risk (fix the cytopenias) vs higher risk (alter the natural history)
docs.text: Myelodysplastic syndromes Clonal stem-cell disorders with ineffective hematopoiesis → cytopenias, dysplasia, and variable AML risk · blasts <20% · everything collapses to lower risk (fix the cytopenias) vs higher risk (alter the natural history) Compiled from the Encyclopedia MDS review note and Fellowship Anki deck · WHO 2022 / ICC · IPSS-M (Bernard, NEJM Evid 2022) · Bernard/Papaemmanuil molecular taxonomy (Blood 2024) Diagnosis Triad: (1) cytopenia + (2) morphologic dysplasia in >10% of a lineage + (3) clonality (cytogenetic or molecular). >90% show clonality on karyotype/NGS Normal marrow cellularity ≈ 100 − age . Most MDS is hypercellular with ineffective hematopoiesis; a hypoplastic variant overlaps aplastic anemia Dysplasia is not MDS without clonality. Exclude mimics first: B12, folate, copper deficiency, HIV, alcohol, medications, post-chemotherapy marrow recovery † Hypoplastic MDS overlaps aplastic anemia and PNH — send flow for a PNH clone † Consider VEXAS (somatic UBA1 ) in older men with inflammatory features, macrocytic anemia and vacuoles in myeloid and erythroid precursors Classification (WHO 2022 / ICC) Genetically defined SF3B1 (favorable, ring sideroblasts) · isolated del(5q) (lenalidomide-responsive) · biallelic TP53 (poor) Blast categories MDS-IB1 = 5–9% blasts · MDS-IB2 = 10–19% The AML border At 10–19% blasts with a defining lesion , ICC calls it MDS/AML (managed as AML) while WHO calls it MDS-IB2 † del(5q) phenotype Macrocytic anemia, normal or high platelets , hypolobated megakaryocytes, female predominance Risk stratification IPSS-R (2012) Cytogenetic risk, marrow blast %, hemoglobin, platelets, ANC → 5 groups IPSS-M (2022) Keeps blasts, Hgb, platelets, cytogenetics · drops ANC · adds 31 gene mutations → 6 groups Mutation weights TP53-multihit highest risk · SF3B1 favorable · adverse: ASXL1, RUNX1, SRSF2, U2AF1, EZH2, FLT3, KMT2A-PTD Calculator at mds-risk-model.com. IPSS-M still outperforms a purely molecular-subgroup model, so use it for risk scoring. Molecular taxonomy (Bernard/Papaemmanuil, Blood 2024). 3,233 patients, 152-gene panel → 16 molecular groups covering 86%, median OS ranging 0.9–8.2 years . Favorable: SF3B1 (14%, most common, OS ~6 yr) · del(5q) · CCUS-like · ZRSR2 · driver-negative. Monocytic: bi-TET2 (13%, CMML overlap). Aggressive: AML-like (OS ~0.9 yr, 40% 2-yr AML transformation) · TP53-complex · IDH-STAG2 · −7/SETBP1 · EZH2-ASXL1 · BCOR. DDX41: high blasts and high transformation but no excess mortality . Take-home: the prognostic weight of blast % depends on genetic subtype — but IPSS-M still outperforms a groups-only model, so the taxonomy informs biology rather than replacing risk scoring.
